abstract: Service value chains are expanding faster than industrial ones, yet their geography is strikingly different: a US-centred star rather than regional blocs. This column documents the shift from factories to offices and argues that differences in production processes call for new theory, new empirical approaches, and new development thinking.

abstract: The European Commission is simplifying the rules around the EU energy label. This column uses product-level sales data on refrigerators in Belgium, France, Germany, and Poland to evaluate the impact on energy use of the 2021 switch from the inflated A+++/A++/A+ scale to a more informative A–G scale. Although consumers prefer better-rated products, they value one euro of future electricity costs at only 42–79 cents. Relabeling alone reduces average electricity use per refrigerator sold by 0.7–2.2%, but other policies would be more effective: a revenue-neutral feebate would reduce electricity use by 2–6% and a stricter minimum standard by 10–16%, at the cost of higher prices.
authors: Toker Doganoglu, Lukasz Grzybowski, Frank Verboven
title: Energy labels, feebates and standards: Lessons from the EU’s 2021 reform

abstract: The redirection of Chinese exports away from the US has fuelled concerns about its spillovers to other countries. This column shows why trade-basket similarity can be a misleading measure of exposure and introduces four simple, theory-consistent indices: export competition, import competition, consumer gains, and sourcing gains. They produce different country rankings and reveal how competitive losses can coexist with gains from cheaper goods and inputs. Thus, the response to spillovers from the surge in Chinese exports should be guided by where the shock actually lands, not by which countries look most like China.
authors: Pol Antràs, Adrian Kulesza, Andrea Presbitero
